title: The Artificial Intelligence Cognitive Examination: A Survey on the Evolution of Multimodal Evaluation From Recognition to Reasoning

bias_targets.methodology: Altering the distribution of question-answer pairs between training and testing splits (e.g., VQA-CP benchmark) to penalize models that rely on statistical text correlations rather than genuine visual grounding.
Permuting multiple-choice options during evaluation (e.g., CircularEval in MMBench) to measure whether a model disproportionately prefers certain answer positions (e.g., defaulting to Option A).
Analyzing model accuracy disparities on non-Western images, non-English contexts, and cross-cultural visual concepts to expose Western-centric dataset representations.

Evaluating model performance on explicitly negated prompts and statements (e.g., using NegBench or NegVQA) to test if models systematically fail to correctly interpret negative phrasing and default to affirmative responses.
Applying out-of-distribution (OOD) visual perturbations and image corruptions (e.g., ImageNet-C) to expose and measure a model's reliance on superficial texture features over semantic shape.

Employing human-in-the-loop red-teaming, analyzing responses to violence-provoking speech, and utilizing embodied simulators with controlled diversity variables (e.g., varying avatar skin tones) to probe toxic or stereotypical outputs.
